objective: Request auto-merge only for the intended dev PR at the exact independently reviewed and validated head.
acceptanceCriteria:
Wrong repository/base/head, failed or pending checks, unresolved review threads, absent independent review or high-risk approval all produce zero merge writes.
A head change between check and request is rejected by the merge command.
Disabled auto-merge and absent effective gate policy leave an actionable blocker, never done.
Queued merge stays distinguishable from observed merged; repeated completion checks are idempotent.
nonGoals: Do not enable branch protection/auto-merge, merge unreviewed work or redesign project test execution.
risks: risk:high: Resolve repository/issue/PR association from prepared context plus GitHub; require base=dev, open non-draft PR, matching head SHA and head-bound validation receipts. Read repository merge settings, effective branch/ruleset requirements, required check conclusions and PR review/thread state. Missing/unreadable gate policy fails closed; never use --admin or enable settings. Require an independent review receipt bound to head and reviewer identity, distinct from implementation provenance; where repository policy demands GitHub approval, require GitHub approval as well. High-risk plan approval must name the approved plan revision and cannot be inferred from a ready label. Pass the expected head to the merge request to reject head-change races. Keep issue in review while merge is queued; on a later bounded idempotent review/completion check, mark done only after GitHub reports merged. Do not add a blocking polling loop. Keep required-check names policy-driven; tests use fake effective policy. Current missing production gates are a rollout blocker, not permission to synthesize passing evidence.
suggestedWorkBreakdown:
Build a read-only eligibility check with a structured allow/deny receipt listing evidence and exact SHA.
Wire it as a workflow command before merge routing, with no agent-owned GitHub state edits.
Make routing consume the receipt, request merge with head protection, and distinguish queued/merged/refused outcomes.
Add bounded completion reconciliation to the existing review path and preserve mutually exclusive lifecycle labels.
unresolvedQuestions: Awaiting explicit human approval of the recorded high-risk plan.
